taxonomy:
## Taxonomy (taxonomy of grid-based logic games by shared rule-types)

### A. Illumination / Visibility line-of-sight
- **Akari**: Place bulbs so every white cell is illuminated in row/column until a black square or outer frame; bulbs must not illuminate each other.
  
### B. Drawing a single closed loop through cells/dots
- **Dotchi-Loop**: Single loop through cell centers; must pass all white-circle cells with area consistency; must avoid black-circle cells.
- **Mid-loop**: Single loop; must pass all black circles with a “midpoint of straight segment” constraint.
- **Masyu**: Single loop; black/white circles impose turning-straight behavior at/around circles.
- **Nagareru**: Single continuous loop; direction comes from arrows; loop movement constrained by wind direction until hitting border/black cells.
- **Moon-or-Sun**: Single loop; rooms visited at most once; in each room must use either all moon cells or all sun cells.
- **Suraromu**: Single loop; must pass all gates exactly once; start/end at marked open circle; gate numbers constrain crossing order.
- **Slitherlink**: Single loop along grid dots; each number indicates how many sides of the cell are surrounded by loop.
- **Yajilin**: Single loop through cell centers; must avoid black cells and numbered cells; numbered cells constrain direction.
- **Yosenabe**: Movement arrows/lines/loop are not used; excluded (taxonomy item only includes true loop-drawing games).
  
### C. Connectivity / paths / networks (lines connecting points or forming continuous structures)
- **Hashiwokakero**: Connect numbered islands with bridges; bridges max 2 between islands; bridges cannot cross islands/bridges; all islands connected.
- **Numberlink**: Connect equal-number pairs with non-branching non-crossing paths through cells; lines cannot go through other numbers.

### D. Coloring / shading regions with rectangle/square constraints
- **Choco Banana**: Paint some cells black; black connected component(s) must form rectangles/squares; white components must not form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate component size.
- **Heyawake**: Rooms contain a count of painted cells; painted cells cannot connect; white cells cannot span more than two rooms in a straight line; white cells not separated by painted cells.
- **Hitori**: Color cells black so duplicates in any row/column are removed; black cells cannot touch; white cells form a continuous network.
- **Kurodoko**: Shade cells black with non-touching black cells; numbered cells forced white; all white cells connected; numbers count white cells until next black/frame.
- **Kurotto**: Circles indicate sum of continuous black-cell runs in both axes through the circle; circles cannot be colored.
- **LITS**: Tetromino-like placements in bold-bordered areas; similarly shaped pieces cannot touch except at corners; colored squares must be connected; no 2×2+ colored block.
- **Nurikabe**: Non-number cells are black/white with constraints: numbers give size of white components; black cells form continuous wall; black cells cannot form 2×2.
- **Nuritwin**: Each outlined region contains exactly two same-size blocks of shaded cells (by number); blocks in a region cannot touch orthogonally; no fully shaded 2×2; all shaded cells connected across regions.
- **Sto-stone**: “Drop” stones; regions (“Rooms”) constrain number of continuous black cells; black cells not connected across bold lines; after dropping, bottom half filled without empty cells.
- **Usowan**: Colorable cells with numbers constraints; numbered cells cannot be colored; numbers count colored neighbors orthogonally with “one wrong number per bold rectangle”.
- **Yajilin / Yosenabe / others**: not included here because they are loop/move-based rather than generic shading-with-rectangular constraints.

### E. Wall / maze / separation constraints
- **Hashiwokakero**: (bridges; connectivity rather than wall maze) excluded here.
- **Nurimeizu**: Paint walls to create a maze from S to G using only white cells; rooms (bold-bordered) constraints; white cells cannot be cut off into loops; some special symbols’ rooms cannot be painted; no 2×2+ coverage by black/white rules.
- **Ripple Effect**: Numbered rooms with consecutive numbers; rooms separated by bold lines; constraint on spacing when duplicates occur in a row/column.
- **Satogaeri**: Move circles within “countries” (bold-bordered regions) so each country has only one circle; circles have pass-through counts; circles can’t cross other circles’ tracks or go over circles.

### F. Tiling / covering / placing fixed polyomino-like shapes
- **Double Choco**: Grid partitioned into blocks by solid lines; each block contains two congruent (possibly rotated/reflected) regions of white and gray; block number equals half the total cells of the block’s color.
- **Evolomino**: Place a growing chain-like set of numbers on arrow paths: each arrow must pass through blocks; blocks extend by adding one square without rotation/flip.
- **LITS**: Tetromino placement under non-touch constraints (also fits tiling/shape category).
- **Shakashaka**: Place black triangles of several orientations in squares; uncovered white area must form rectangles/squares; numbers indicate count of surrounding black triangles orthogonally.
- **Shikaku**: Partition grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains only one number equal to its area (cell count).

### G. Partitioning / grouping cells into blocks (size and adjacency rules)
- **Chained Block**: Blocks are maximal consecutive black-cell runs; each block has one number or “?”; all blocks must be part of a chain; chain forbids having more than one block of identical size/shape up to rotation/mirror.
- **Five Cells**: Partition into blocks of exactly 5 cells; numbers indicate line counts around cells including outer frame; lines surround cells and cannot enter a block.
- **Fillomino**: Fill grid with numbers so each block contains exactly that many cells; blocks of equal size cannot touch orthogonally.
- **Chained Block** already included here (block-based black-cell chains).
  
### H. Numeric placement with standard Sudoku-like constraints (rows/columns + subblocks)
- **Sudoku**: Place 1–9; each row/column and each bold 3×3 block contains all digits 1–9.

### I. “Loop + gate/turning/straight” hybrid variants (still loop-based, but distinctly constrained)
(covered largely in category B; retained here if separating “turning/turn rules” vs generic loop)
- **Masyu**, **Suraromu**, **Moon-or-Sun**, **Yajilin**, **Dotchi-Loop**, **Nagareru**, **Mid-loop**, **Slitherlink**.

### J. Snake/territorial sequential placement
- **Hebi**: Place sequence numbers 1→5 as connected snake parts in white squares; snakes cannot touch orthogonally; direction-of-view constraints from arrow black squares and nearest-number counts; “0” means no snake until next black/frame.
  
### K. Directional path drawing from tips/knots (non-loop)
- **Pencils**: Pencils are straight sequences from a tip (one end); numbered pencil cells give length; the traced line must pass through required number of cells; no self-cross or branching.

### L. Movement of tokens into regions / avoidance of crossing tracks
- **Satogaeri**: Move circles within countries; each country ends with exactly one circle; movement lengths constrained by numbers; no crossing tracks of other circles and no passing over other circles.
- **Yosenabe**: Move circles orthogonally into gray areas without bending; arrows show straight movement; arrows don’t cross other white circles or other arrows’ lines; each gray area sum constraint equals incoming circles’ numbers.

### M. Equality/comparison in rows/columns/intervals
- **Juosan**: Fill grid with “—” or “|” marks; bold-bordered territories: counts of extra “—” or “|” marks relative to given numbers; marks extend with maximum run lengths horizontally/vertically depending on “—”/“|”.
- **Heyawake** partly belongs here but is primarily separation/room/paint connectivity.

### N. Numberlink-like path connectivity (already in C)
- **Numberlink**: included in C.

### O. Mixed “rooms/constraints” including arithmetic about neighborhoods
- **Tilepaint**: Bold-bordered tiles; diagonal-line numbers constrain count of black cells to right/down along line/column until boundary/next diagonal; all cells in a tile either all colored or all uncolored.
- **Usowan**: Local neighborhood counts of colored cells with exactly one “wrong number” per bold rectangle.
